editorial:
Imagine waking up to the news that a dangerous killer just broke out of a high-security asylum and is roaming the streets of London. That is exactly how you get pulled into this story. You follow Frank Norton, a man struggling with schizophrenia who is on a violent path of destruction. The whole thing happens over one scary night, and the tension builds fast once Frank grabs a hostage. It feels like a high-stakes game where you are constantly wondering if the victim will find a way out or if the killer is just too far gone to stop. 

The acting is solid and keeps you on edge, though some parts of the plot feel a bit predictable if you have seen a lot of thrillers. The pacing is quick, so you will not get bored, but the low budget shows in a few scenes. If you love movies that make your heart race, you should definitely give this a try. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you want the best picture possible, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the gritty details of the city.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with a tense showdown between Frank and his hostage. As the police close in, you find out that Frank's actions were driven by his distorted view of reality. In the end, the cat-and-mouse game reaches a breaking point where Frank is finally stopped. The twist lies in how his mind worked throughout the night, showing that he wasn't just random, but following a dark logic in his own head.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cat-and-mouse chase movies and psychological thrillers.
